questions.question: Every box has which three adjustable rings around the content?
questions.explanation: Every box has three available properties: border, margin, and padding.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Every box has three available properties that can be adjusted to control its appearance:

questions.question: Where does margin sit?
options: Outside the edge of the border.
questions.explanation: Margins sit outside the edge of the border. You can set the width of a margin to create a gap between boxes.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Margins sit outside the edge of the border.

questions.question: What is padding?
options: The gap between two neighbors' borders.
The space between the border of a box and any content contained within it.
The outline drawn by the browser chrome.
questions.explanation: Padding is the space between the border of a box and any content contained within it.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Padding is the space between the border of a box and any content contained within it.

questions.question: The padding property specifies space between?
options: The content of an element and its border.
The viewport and the html element only.
questions.explanation: The padding property allows you to specify how much space should appear between the content of an element and its border.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: how much space should appear between the content of an element and its border.

questions.question: In the default box model, width is?
options: The content box. Padding and border add extra.
questions.explanation: Figure 3.4 is the default box model: width/height on the content, then padding, border, margin.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: Grant's sidebar example overflows because?
options: 30% plus left/right padding plus 70% is more than 100%.
Margins cannot be used on floats.
questions.explanation: The sidebar has width 30% plus 1.5em left and right padding; main is 70%. Total is 100% plus 3em.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: This brings the total of the two columns to 100% plus 3 ems.

questions.question: What does box-sizing: border-box change?
options: Padding doesn't make the element wider; it makes the inner content narrower.
questions.explanation: With border-box, padding doesn't make an element wider; it makes the inner content narrower. Same for height.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: padding doesn’t make an element wider; it makes the inner content narrower.

questions.question: What is a magic number in this chapter?
options: 26% because it looked right on one screen.
questions.explanation: A width of 26% for the sidebar works on the author's screen but is unreliable. That 26% is a magic number.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The 26% is known as a magic number.

questions.question: Which rule keeps 30% including padding?
questions.explanation: border-box means the declared width includes padding and border.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: If you update these elements to use border box sizing, they’ll fit on the same line

questions.question: Does every box have a border even at 0?
options: No. border is optional and absent until set.
Yes. Every box has a border, even if it is not visible or is 0 pixels wide.
questions.explanation: Every box has a border (even if it is not visible or is specified to be 0 pixels wide).

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Every box has a border (even if it is not visible or is specified to be 0 pixels wide).

questions.question: Which creates a gap between two boxes?
questions.explanation: Set the width of a margin to create a gap between the borders of two boxes.

questions.question: Grant's layout chapter is built on?
options: Document flow and the box model — the basic rules for position and size.
questions.explanation: Advanced layout sits on document flow and the box model; these are the basic rules that determine position and size.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: Which calc() matches Grant's gutter idea?
questions.explanation: Subtract the gutter from the width: calc(30% - 1.5em), then margin-left: 1.5em.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: padding: 10px 15px 0 — what is the right side?
questions.explanation: Shorthand is top, right, bottom, left. Three values: top, horizontal, bottom. Right is 15px.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: Why is trial-and-error 26% a poor width?
options: You won't know how it behaves on another viewport.
questions.explanation: If you don't understand where the number comes from, you won't understand how it will behave under different circumstances.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
